checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add details.py (file facts always; dimensions, camera, lens, exposure, aperture, ISO and focal length with optional Pillow); GET /api/details/<sha> with the same visibility as media; viewer Details panel; tests, dogfood, ADR-012, README

impact_assessment.why: The viewer shows only name, date and size; users cannot see dimensions or camera settings, and the data is already in the file
impact_assessment.benefits: One click shows capture facts; no schema change, no index, no extra dependency beyond the optional Pillow already used for previews and dates
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new read-only endpoint and viewer control; dependency: Pillow optional, HEIC via pillow-heif; concurrency: on-demand file read, no shared mutable state; state: none persisted
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read only the requested original through the store's visibility check, cache nothing, catch unreadable EXIF, and return file facts even when Pillow is absent or the image is a video

checkpoints.description: [2/4] details.py returns file facts always and dimensions/EXIF with Pillow; pillow_support.py now centralizes optional Pillow+HEIC loading for previews, dates and details; 3 unit tests

[3/4] GET /api/details/<sha> follows media visibility; viewer Details panel shows file facts, dates, dimensions, camera, lens, exposure, aperture, ISO and focal length; browser dogfood verified a 20x10 JPEG with Acme EXIF, 0 JS errors
[4/4] 114 tests; 4/4 project gates; README prerequisites, how-it-works and API; ADR-012; codebase map regenerated; checklists: passed
Task 'photo-details' completed successfully.

[1/5] Plan: selection.py centralizes bulk hash validation; downloads.py builds a stored zip in .harbor/downloads with size/free-space caps and one-time expiring tokens; POST /api/download {sha256s|album} returns a URL; GET /api/download/<token> serves and deletes; Reply delete_after; UI Download in the selection bar and album scope; tests, dogfood, ADR-013, README

impact_assessment.why: Albums and selection can collect photos, but taking them out still means opening and downloading originals one at a time
impact_assessment.benefits: One zip for a trip, album or selection; no recompression, no second copy of the library, and no schema change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new endpoint, token store and Reply cleanup; dependency: stdlib zipfile only; concurrency: token map and temp file creation under a lock; state: temporary zips and expiry
impact_assessment.mitigation: Cap batches at 500 hashes and 8 GiB, require free space, use random one-time tokens with a 15-minute expiry, delete after send or on startup, and sanitize zip entry names

checkpoints.description: [2/5] selection.py owns bulk hash parsing/validation; downloads.py builds stored ZIPs with duplicate-name handling, 8 GiB and free-space checks, profile-bound one-time tokens and 15-minute expiry; 5 unit tests
[3/5] POST /api/download {sha256s|album} and GET /api/download/<token>; Reply.delete_after removes the ZIP in a finally; HTTP tests cover selection, album, one-time use, auth and no leftover file
[4/5] Selection bar Download and album Download album; 500-photo selection cap with album fallback; browser dogfood downloaded both ZIPs and verified one.png inside, 0 JS errors
[5/5] 120 tests; 4/4 project gates; README, limits and API; ADR-013; codebase map regenerated; checklists: passed
Task 'bulk-download' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: Catalog.storage returns file counts, bytes, photo/video split, shared-photo count, per-person shares and the ten largest files; GET /api/storage keeps the same profile visibility; Sync tab panel with summary, people and largest files; tests, dogfood, ADR-014, README

impact_assessment.why: The Sync tab shows only a total count and bytes; users cannot see which person takes the space or what the largest files are, and hard-link savings are invisible
impact_assessment.benefits: One read-only report for disk planning; owner sees everyone, each person sees only their own share; no schema change and no file reads
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new read-only endpoint; dependency: none; concurrency: three aggregate queries per request; state: none persisted
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep it to indexed aggregates and ten rows, scope every query to the visible profile, and show only names and sizes the caller may already see

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Catalog.storage reports whole-library or per-person counts, bytes, photo/video split, shared photos, per-person shares and ten largest files; 2 unit tests
[3/4] GET /api/storage with the same visibility as status; HTTP test proves the owner sees 2 people and a person sees only their one file, with ?profile=main refused
[4/4] Sync Storage panel shows summary, shared count, per-person shares and largest files with links; browser dogfood 2 files, 2 people, 2 largest, 0 JS errors
[4/4] 123 tests; 4/4 project gates; README/API/tree; ADR-014; codebase map regenerated; checklists: passed
Task 'storage-report' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: album rail rows show their newest photo as a cover; the selection Add-to-album menu offers New album…, creates it and adds the selected batch in chunks; dogfood, README, ADR-015

impact_assessment.why: Albums are listed as text and creating one while photos are selected sends the user back to the sidebar and loses the selection
impact_assessment.benefits: Covers make albums recognizable; one flow collects a trip without leaving selection mode; no backend contract change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none server-side; dependency: cover thumbnails use the existing /thumb route; concurrency: none; state: selection remains client-only
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse the existing albums and batch endpoints, keep the 500-hash chunking, and fall back to a text row when a cover or thumbnail is unavailable

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Album rail rows show a lazy cover with text fallback; selection Add-to-album menu starts with New album…, creates it and adds the selection in 500-hash chunks
[3/3] Browser dogfood created the album from the selection, saw the rail cover, downloaded selection and album; 123 tests, 4/4 gates; README/ADR-015; checklists: passed
